metadata.description: A course-scale inventory of publicly accessible aquatic and wetland sites in Toronto and Mississauga that offer defensible settings for duck and waterfowl viewing.
metadata.coordinate_note: Coordinates are representative map points for each named public site, habitat feature or practical viewing area. They are suitable for a regional Leaflet assignment, but are not survey-grade. Coordinates were cross-checked against OpenStreetMap/Nominatim place records and official site maps where available.
metadata.selection_note: Sites were selected from official municipal, conservation-authority and park-operator descriptions of public access, birding, waterfowl, wetlands or aquatic habitat. A site is not a promise that ducks will be present on a particular visit.
metadata.responsible_viewing_note: Stay on signed paths and viewing platforms, obey closures, keep dogs leashed where required, do not feed wildlife and do not approach nests or restricted habitat.
metadata.geojson_use: Load this file with fetch(), parse it as JSON, and pass the resulting FeatureCollection to L.geoJSON().

properties.name: Grenadier Pond – High Park
properties.waterbody: Grenadier Pond
properties.access: Public City park; shoreline paths and designated pond-edge areas are accessible from High Park entrances. Follow current park and vehicle-access signs.
properties.description: A large naturalized pond and lakeside-marsh remnant within High Park, with public shoreline viewpoints and established bird habitat.
properties.selection_basis: City sources describe Grenadier Pond as environmentally significant wildlife habitat and High Park as supporting Wood Duck and diverse migrant and breeding birds.

properties.name: Humber Bay Park East
properties.waterbody: Lake Ontario and Humber Bay Park East pond/wetland
properties.access: Public waterfront park with paths and boardwalks; the park reopened in July 2026, though finishing work may affect small areas.
properties.description: A Lake Ontario peninsula with sheltered water, a revitalized pond and linear wetland, and multiple public shoreline viewpoints.
properties.selection_basis: City planning documents identify Humber Bay Park as a major Toronto location for observing overwintering waterfowl and describe wetland and pond habitat in the east park.

properties.name: Colonel Samuel Smith Park
properties.waterbody: Lake Ontario bays and marina embayment
properties.access: Public City park with a network of waterfront paths; observe wildlife from paths and open shoreline viewpoints.
properties.description: A lakefill waterfront park combining bays, marshes, meadows and open Lake Ontario shoreline.
properties.selection_basis: The City identifies the park as a premier birding destination and specifically notes winter waterfowl associated with its bays, marshes and marina area.

properties.name: Toronto Islands – Snug Harbour
properties.waterbody: Toronto Islands lagoons and Snug Harbour
properties.access: Public island park reached by ferry or water taxi; use signed multi-use paths and bridges. Ferry service and facilities vary by season.
properties.description: A sheltered harbour and lagoon setting within the Toronto Islands, surrounded by public paths and linked island habitats.
properties.selection_basis: The City lists Snug Harbour among key Toronto Islands bird-watching areas and describes the island lagoon network and year-round trails.

properties.name: Tommy Thompson Park
properties.waterbody: Triangle Pond, Cell One wetlands and Lake Ontario embayments
properties.access: Public access is managed by TRCA: weekdays 4 p.m.–9 p.m.; weekends and holidays 5:30 a.m.–9 p.m. Check current notices and respect restricted nesting areas.
properties.description: A large waterfront habitat complex with coastal marshes, created wetlands, ponds, embayments and designated viewing areas.
properties.selection_basis: TRCA explicitly identifies Triangle Pond, wetland cells and embayments as waterfowl-viewing locations and documents functional waterfowl habitat.

properties.name: Centennial Park Pond
properties.waterbody: Centennial Park ponds and Elmcrest Creek wetlands
properties.access: Public City park; use park paths and pond lookouts. Naturalization and construction work may restrict small areas, so follow posted signs.
properties.description: An urban park pond-and-creek system with newly naturalized shorelines, pocket wetlands and adjacent open habitat.
properties.selection_basis: The City documents ponds, wetlands and wetland birds in the park; selection is habitat-based and does not imply reliable duck abundance.

properties.name: Ashbridges Bay Park
properties.waterbody: Ashbridges Bay and Coatsworth Cut
properties.access: Public waterfront park with trails, seating and shoreline viewpoints; stay outside marina and work areas.
properties.description: A partly sheltered Lake Ontario bay with park paths, vegetated shoreline edges and nearby aquatic habitat improvements.
properties.selection_basis: TRCA environmental assessment material identifies the bay as potential habitat used by migrating waterfowl and notes that softer shoreline edges offer better wildlife cover than hardened shorelines.

properties.name: Bluffer's Park
properties.waterbody: Lake Ontario and Bluffer's Park marina basin
properties.access: Public waterfront park with trails, lookouts and shoreline areas; some marina docks are private or seasonally controlled.
properties.description: A Scarborough waterfront park with open lake shoreline, beach, sheltered marina water and public nature-viewing areas.
properties.selection_basis: TRCA identifies bird watching and nature appreciation as park activities; inclusion is based on accessible shoreline and sheltered water rather than a claim of dependable duck sightings.

properties.name: Corktown Common Wetland
properties.waterbody: Corktown Common constructed wetland and ponds
properties.access: Public City park with paved paths and bridges beside the wetland; remain on paths and planted-area edges.
properties.description: A naturalized constructed wetland and pond system embedded in a downtown flood-protection park.
properties.selection_basis: City planning material documents interconnected naturalized ponds, aquatic vegetation and pedestrian access; duck-viewing potential is a habitat inference, not a reported count.

properties.name: Don Valley Brick Works Park
properties.waterbody: Evergreen Ponds and Mud Creek
properties.access: Public park trails and pond boardwalks behind Evergreen Brick Works; larger organized groups may require a City permit.
properties.description: A restored former quarry with connected ponds, wetland vegetation, boardwalks and public birding opportunities.
properties.selection_basis: Evergreen's birding guidance names Wood Duck among birds to look for around the Brick Works wetlands, while City material identifies wetland habitat at the site.

properties.name: James Gardens and Lambton Woods
properties.waterbody: Humber River and spring-fed park ponds
properties.access: Public City park with riverside trail connections, garden paths and a scenic Humber Valley lookout.
properties.description: A Humber River valley park with spring-fed pools, streams, mature riparian habitat and connections into Lambton Woods.
properties.selection_basis: The City's bird guide identifies the broader Lambton Woods/James Gardens area as breeding habitat used by Wood Duck in the past.

properties.name: Port Union Waterfront Park
properties.waterbody: Lake Ontario between Highland Creek and the Rouge River
properties.access: Public waterfront trail and lookouts. In November 2026 the eastern cobble shoreline is fenced for repair, with a signed trail detour; most of the park remains open.
properties.description: A long public Lake Ontario shoreline park with headlands, cobble shore, creek-mouth connections and created aquatic habitat.
properties.selection_basis: TRCA documents additional aquatic habitat, public lookouts and a shoreline wildlife corridor; duck-viewing potential is habitat-based rather than a reported observation claim.

properties.name: Kariya Park
properties.waterbody: Kariya Park duck pond and ornamental marsh
properties.access: Public City park, generally open daily 7 a.m.–11 p.m.; use the boardwalks and paths around the water features.
properties.description: A compact Japanese-inspired urban park with a named duck pond, ornamental marsh, boardwalk and waterfall.
properties.selection_basis: The City documents a duck pond and marsh as public park features; the name describes the feature and is not evidence of guaranteed duck presence.

properties.name: Rattray Marsh Conservation Area
properties.waterbody: Rattray Marsh, Sheridan Creek and Lake Ontario
properties.access: Free public access from after sunrise to before sunset; parking is at Jack Darling Memorial Park. Stay on trails and boardwalks.
properties.description: A natural lakefront marsh with boardwalks, forest trails, mudflats and a rocky Lake Ontario shoreline.
properties.selection_basis: Credit Valley Conservation explicitly identifies ducks and other waterfowl in the marsh and along the shoreline and promotes the site for birdwatching.

properties.name: Jim Tovey Lakeview Conservation Area
properties.waterbody: Serson Wetland, Applewood Wetland and Lake Ontario
properties.access: Public trails and lookouts; enter from Marie Curtis Park. There is no on-site visitor parking, and sensitive restoration areas may close periodically.
properties.description: A restored waterfront conservation area with coastal wetlands, creeks, boardwalks and accessible birdwatching lookouts.
properties.selection_basis: Credit Valley Conservation describes coastal wetlands and birdwatching, including mallards as a species visitors may encounter; this does not guarantee a sighting.

properties.name: Lake Wabukayne
properties.waterbody: Lake Wabukayne stormwater pond
properties.access: Public City park, open daily from dawn until 11 p.m.; a walking trail circles the pond and connects to Lake Aquitaine.
properties.description: A 1.8-hectare stormwater-management pond with a floating island, surrounding trail and naturalized park habitat.
properties.selection_basis: The City promotes nature and bird watching at the pond and separately notes that waterfowl are common near lakes and ponds in Mississauga parks.

properties.name: Lake Aquitaine Park
properties.waterbody: Lake Aquitaine stormwater pond
properties.access: Public City park, open daily from dawn until 11 p.m.; trails and a fishing dock provide water views.
properties.description: A man-made stormwater pond surrounded by public trails and park facilities in Meadowvale.
properties.selection_basis: The City identifies Lake Aquitaine as one of Mississauga's waterfront and pond settings associated with returning waterfowl; no abundance is asserted here.

properties.name: Osprey Marsh
properties.waterbody: Osprey Marsh
properties.access: Public City park, open daily from dawn until 11 p.m.; the paved loop connects with Lisgar Meadow Brook and Britannia trails.
properties.description: An accessible urban marsh with a paved loop, benches and nesting boxes beside wetland habitat.
properties.selection_basis: The City promotes Osprey Marsh for bird watching and wildlife viewing and identifies it among Mississauga migration-viewing locations.

properties.name: Saigon Park
properties.waterbody: Saigon Park stormwater pond
properties.access: Public City park, open daily from dawn until 11 p.m.; a one-kilometre trail and pier provide pond viewpoints.
properties.description: A large stormwater pond with naturalized plantings, public trails, lookout points and a viewing pier.
properties.selection_basis: The City lists Saigon Park among migration-viewing locations and among stormwater ponds associated with returning waterfowl.

properties.name: Lakefront Promenade Park
properties.waterbody: Lake Ontario and Lakefront Promenade marina basin
properties.access: Public City park, open daily from dawn until 11 p.m.; use the waterfront pathway, beach and public shoreline areas.
properties.description: A Lake Ontario waterfront park with exposed shoreline, sheltered marina water and a continuous public pathway.
properties.selection_basis: The City identifies Lakefront Promenade as a migration-viewing location and as a waterfront setting associated with returning waterfowl.

properties.name: Jack Darling Memorial Park
properties.waterbody: Lake Ontario shoreline beside Rattray Marsh
properties.access: Public City park, open daily from dawn until 11 p.m.; waterfront paths connect directly to Rattray Marsh boardwalk trails.
properties.description: A public Lake Ontario shoreline park next to Rattray Marsh, with beach, waterfront trail and natural areas.
properties.selection_basis: The City promotes the Jack Darling–Rattray area for birdwatching and identifies Jack Darling among waterfront locations associated with returning waterfowl.

properties.name: Riverwood
properties.waterbody: Credit River, wetlands and park creeks
properties.access: Public City park, open daily from dawn until 11 p.m.; accessible trails and garden overlooks provide wetland and river views.
properties.description: A large urban nature park containing Credit River frontage, wetlands, creeks, ravines, meadows and mature forest.
properties.selection_basis: The City documents extensive bird diversity, wetlands and the Credit River at Riverwood and identifies the park as a migration-viewing location.

properties.name: Meadowvale Conservation Area
properties.waterbody: Credit River and associated wetland complex
properties.access: Public City-managed conservation park, open daily from dawn until 11 p.m.; use trails, riverbanks and the pedestrian bridge.
properties.description: A broad Credit River valley conservation area with river flats, wetland complex, trails and public bridge viewpoints.
properties.selection_basis: City sources identify Meadowvale Conservation Area for bird migration viewing and document a public river-valley wetland complex.

properties.name: Erindale Park
properties.waterbody: Credit River
properties.access: Public City park, open daily from dawn until 11 p.m.; extensive trails provide river and ravine views.
properties.description: Mississauga's largest park, with public trails following the Credit River through ravine and riparian habitat.
properties.selection_basis: The City explicitly promotes the park for bird and nature watching beside the Credit River; inclusion does not assert duck abundance.

properties.name: Creditview Wetland
properties.waterbody: Creditview Wetland
properties.access: Public trail access from Fallingbrook Drive, reached from the Eglinton Avenue Trail or Bristol Road bike lanes; view from the wooden platform and remain on paths.
properties.description: A compact provincially significant urban wetland with a public viewing platform and rare marsh vegetation.
properties.selection_basis: The City explicitly describes the viewing platform as a place to view nesting waterfowl and documents the wetland's ecological significance.
